title: geolocator
objectives: Understand geolocator via a real-life analogy
Request + verify location permission on both platforms
Pick the right accuracy vs battery trade-off
Stream position updates + handle background limits

sections.markdown:
**Think of geolocator as the GPS antenna + a very talkative doorman.**

The GPS chip on the phone is a shared resource. The OS makes you knock politely — declare intent, ask permission, tell it how sharp you need the fix + how often. In return you get positions.

- **Accuracy trade-off** — `LocationAccuracy.high` = live GPS (2-5 s TTFF; ~1% battery per hour). `medium` = network + cell (~10 m). `low` = cell only (~1 km, cheap). Match to use case: rider tracking = high; nearby-shops = medium.
- **Permission tiers** — iOS 'When in Use' vs 'Always'; Android FINE vs COARSE (Android 12+ user can even choose 'Approximate only').
- **Background** — iOS suspends most background updates; Android 10+ needs a foreground service for continuous. `geolocator` gives you the API but the OS decides delivery.
- **Distances + bearings** — `Geolocator.distanceBetween(...)` handles the haversine math + returns meters.

**Why every location-aware Flutter app installs it:** wraps the platform boilerplate (permission dance, service availability, position stream) into one Dart API. Even if you use FusedLocationProvider (Android) or CLLocationManager (iOS) natively for advanced use cases, `geolocator` remains the go-to for reading a single position or streaming updates in the foreground.

**`geolocator`** wraps native location services: Android's **FusedLocationProviderClient** (Google Play Services) or `LocationManager` fallback, iOS's **CLLocationManager**, and Web's Geolocation API. Exposes: `checkPermission`, `requestPermission`, `isLocationServiceEnabled`, `getCurrentPosition`, `getLastKnownPosition`, `getPositionStream(LocationSettings)`, `distanceBetween`, `bearingBetween`, `openLocationSettings`, `openAppSettings`.

sections.markdown: ## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Requesting permission without the manifest / Info.plist entries.** iOS silently returns denied; Android throws. Wire manifests first.
**Mistake 2: Ignoring `LocationServiceDisabled`.** GPS off → all requests fail. Check `isLocationServiceEnabled` + prompt to enable.
**Mistake 3: Using `LocationAccuracy.best` everywhere.** Battery drain. Match accuracy to the task.
**Mistake 4: Not stopping the stream.** `_sub` alive after screen leaves = wake locks / battery drain. Cancel in `dispose`.

**Mistake 5: Assuming background delivery.** iOS suspends silently; Android 10+ requires foreground service + notification. For always-on delivery you need `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` + user opts into 'Allow all the time.'
**Mistake 6: No `timeLimit` on `getCurrentPosition`.** In a subway / basement, the request hangs forever. Set 10-15 s and fall back to `getLastKnownPosition`.
**Mistake 7: Precision leak.** Storing sub-centimeter coordinates for a use case that needs neighborhood accuracy → PII risk + unnecessary DB size. Round when appropriate.
**Mistake 8: 'Approximate location' surprise (Android 12+).** User can grant only coarse; your app sees ~200 m error even with FINE requested. Handle gracefully.
## Best practices
**1. Full permission dance** — service + permission + Always vs When in Use + Approximate. Show explainer UI first-time.
**2. Match accuracy to task** — don't burn battery with `best` when `medium` suffices.
**3. Cancel streams in `dispose`.** Every subscription released.
**4. `distanceFilter` + `intervalDuration`** — throttle updates to what UI actually needs.
**5. Android foreground service** — for delivery tracking; user sees a persistent notification (legally required in many jurisdictions).
**6. iOS `activityType`** — hint to the OS (`automotive`, `fitness`, `otherNavigation`) for better filtering + battery.
**7. Fallback to `getLastKnownPosition`** when live fix times out.
**8. Round + throttle stored coordinates** — send only when displacement > threshold; store 5-decimal precision if 1 m suffices.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — One-shot `getCurrentPosition` with full permission flow.
**Practice 2 (Medium)** — Position stream with `distanceFilter=20` + cancel-on-dispose.
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — Compute route length + heading between waypoints.
**Practice 4 (Hard)** — Android foreground-service tracking during a run (fitness app style).
**Practice 5 (Hard)** — Handle user picking 'Approximate only' on Android 12+ — degrade UI.
**Practice 6 (Expert)** — Battery benchmark: high vs medium accuracy vs 30-s interval — measure over 1 h.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: Walk through the full permission dance.**

**A:** **(1) Check location service.** `Geolocator.isLocationServiceEnabled()` — GPS toggle in Settings. If false, `openLocationSettings()` (best UX with rationale). **(2) Check permission.** `checkPermission()` returns `denied / deniedForever / whileInUse / always`. **(3) Request if denied.** `requestPermission()` — first call triggers the system prompt. If user picks 'Deny' → `denied`; 'Don't ask again' → `deniedForever` on Android, or 'Never' on iOS → prompt user to open Settings via `openAppSettings()`. **(4) Handle `whileInUse` vs `always`.** For foreground use, `whileInUse` is fine. For continuous background, iOS requires `always` (and the user must OPT-UP from `whileInUse` in Settings — you can't request Always directly on iOS 14+). **(5) Android 12+ approximate mode.** User can grant only coarse; queries return ~200 m accurate; degrade UI. **(6) Rationale first.** Show a 'why we need this' pre-prompt screen — dramatically improves acceptance rate.

**Q2: How do you get reliable background location tracking?**

**A:** Depends on platform + urgency. **Android:** need a **foreground service** with persistent notification (`ForegroundNotificationConfig` in geolocator's Android settings) + `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` permission + user grants 'Allow all the time.' The service keeps the app process alive; OS won't kill it while the notification is visible. **iOS:** `AppleSettings(pauseLocationUpdatesAutomatically: true, activityType: ActivityType.automotiveNavigation)` + `NSLocationAlwaysUsageDescription` in Info.plist + **background modes → location updates** enabled in Xcode. iOS pauses updates when the app has been static; resumes when the device moves significantly. **Battery honesty:** even with all these, continuous high-accuracy tracking burns ~15% battery per hour on both platforms. **Alternative for less-critical needs:** significant-change notifications (iOS) or geofencing (both) — one-shot triggers on region enter/exit at low battery cost.

**Q3: How do you pick the right `LocationAccuracy`?**

**A:** Match to the USE CASE. **`bestForNavigation`** — turn-by-turn nav: 1-3 m, highest battery. **`high`** — rider tracking, live-share: 5-10 m, high battery. **`medium`** — nearby-shops, weather: 50-100 m, moderate. **`low`** — city/regional offers: 500 m-1 km, cheap. **`lowest`** — timezone hints only. **`reduced`** (iOS 14+, iOS-user picked coarse) — 10 km-ish. **Rule of thumb:** if the UI shows a pin on a map, `high` is the max you need — GPS beyond that is jitter, not precision. For a nearby-list, `medium` is enough. `bestForNavigation` should only run while user is actively driving. Combine with `distanceFilter` (only emit when moved > N meters) and `intervalDuration` (throttle rate) to keep both accuracy AND battery in check.

**Q4: How do you compute distance / bearing correctly?**

**A:** Use `Geolocator.distanceBetween(lat1, lng1, lat2, lng2)` — returns meters via the **haversine formula** (great-circle distance on a sphere). Accurate to ~0.5% for < 100 km distances. **Bearing:** `Geolocator.bearingBetween(...)` returns degrees clockwise from North. **When haversine isn't enough:** > 1000 km / geodetic precision → Vincenty's formula (ellipsoid model); use `latlong2` or `flutter_map`'s helpers. **Rounding pitfall:** doing math on doubles then subtracting nearly-equal values loses precision — order operations to avoid catastrophic cancellation. **Storing:** WGS84 (standard GPS coordinates) is universal; if joining with a backend that stores UTM or MGRS, convert at the boundary. **Anti-pattern:** naive Euclidean `sqrt(dx² + dy²)` on lat/lng — hits accuracy nightmares near poles + at large distances.

**Q5: Location + privacy / GDPR / DPDPA — what to watch?**

**A:** **(1) Consent first.** Explain what you'll do with the location before requesting permission. Consent is required under GDPR / DPDPA / CPRA — permission alone is not consent. **(2) Minimal accuracy.** Store only the precision needed; round to 4 decimals (~10 m) if you don't need finer. **(3) Retention limits.** Don't keep raw tracks forever; aggregate to trip summaries or delete after N days. **(4) Purpose limitation.** Location for delivery = OK; also selling it to ad networks = separate consent required. **(5) Data-subject rights.** User can request export + deletion; design your DB for it. **(6) Cross-border storage** — some regulations require in-country storage of location; check Firebase / your backend regions. **(7) Analytics + location** — Firebase Analytics does NOT log GPS by default; log city-level at most. **(8) Sensitive-location deny-list** — some apps mask locations near shelters / religious sites; considered ethical best practice.

**Q6: What are the platform-specific gotchas?**

**A:** **Android:** (1) `LocationServices` (Play Services) vs `LocationManager` fallback — the plugin uses the fused API on Play Services devices, LocationManager on Huawei / Amazon / non-GMS. (2) `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` is a separate permission on Android 10+ + user must grant 'Allow all the time.' (3) 'Approximate only' on Android 12+ — even with FINE, accuracy drops. (4) Play Console requires justification for background location. **iOS:** (1) Cannot request `always` directly on iOS 14+ — user must upgrade in Settings. (2) `pauseLocationUpdatesAutomatically` + `activityType` for battery savings. (3) `NSLocation*UsageDescription` in Info.plist required per permission type. (4) Background modes → location updates capability. (5) iPad restrictions on GPS in some regions. **Web:** limited API surface; no background; user prompt per session for some browsers. **Windows / macOS:** desktop targets have partial support; test on real hardware.

## Real-world usage

- **Delivery + rider tracking** — foreground service; every 5 s.
- **Nearby discovery** — one-shot medium accuracy.
- **Fitness apps** — activityType `fitness` + foreground service.
- **Weather + timezone** — low accuracy suffices.
- **NOT ideal for** — geofencing (use native + `flutter_background_geolocation` or platform APIs); indoor positioning (Bluetooth beacons).

## Advanced notes

- **`AndroidSettings.foregroundNotificationConfig`** — the plugin manages the foreground service for you.
- **`AppleSettings.activityType`** — hints iOS about your movement pattern for smarter power management.
- **Geofencing** — geolocator itself doesn't do it; use `flutter_background_geolocation` or platform native APIs.
- **`Geolocator.getServiceStatusStream`** — observe user toggling GPS.
- **`getLastKnownPosition`** — instant fallback (may be minutes stale).
- **Mock locations** — Android's mock provider; testers can spoof coords with `set_mock_location`.
- **Web target permission** — synchronous prompt not always possible on some browsers.
- **iOS Simulator location** — set via menu; useful for testing.
- **Location smoothing** — Kalman filter or moving-average to reduce jitter.
- **Battery Health mode** — some devices throttle GPS on low battery; live longer.
- **`ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION`-only apps** — perfectly valid; skip fine if you don't need it (Play Store approval friction).
- **Alternative packages** — `location`, `flutter_background_geolocation`, `background_locator_2`.
